journey.name: TL-06 Undo restores the task, at the bottom, with a new id
journey.description:
Covers FR-12 and the undo semantics REQUIREMENTS.md section 9 spells out (lines 223-225).
TaskApi has no restore operation, so RestoreTaskUseCase re-creates the task. The consequence is deliberate and is the point of this scenario: the restored task gets a new source-assigned id and lands where a newly created task would - at the end of the list, not back in its old slot. Every field the user can see must survive the trip.
A restore is two source calls for a completed task and one for an unfinished one, so the dice are off.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Verify that "Renew domain registration" is the first row in the list
Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Renew domain registration" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Renew domain registration" is on screen again
Verify that "Renew domain registration" is now the last row in the list, below "Migrate the analytics pipeline to the new warehouse and validate dashboards"
Verify that the restored row still has an element with the content description "High"
Verify that the restored row still shows "Due in 3 days"
Verify that four elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
